messages:
marta: Quick PM follow-up - we're still getting waveform-triggered rate-limit pages during low-traffic windows. Looking for a short plan to reduce noise without removing signal.

owen: yep, saw ~90 pages last week at 03:10. Most are thin spikes from retry storms.

priya: idea: make thresholds waveform-aware: compute a 5m traffic baseline per-cluster and require spikes to exceed baseline * multiplier AND an absolute floor before paging. This prevents small bursts during low traffic from paging.

sam: propose multiplier x2 plus absolute floor 50 alerts/min. if baseline < 200 rpm then multiplier x3. Keeps it conservative.

marta: also add dedupe key = client_ip + route + error_code and a dedupe window of 20m for non-prod, 10m for prod. auto-close suppressed duplicates after 25m.

owen: add an SLO override: if error_ratio > 0.5% over 1m then bypass suppression and page immediately. Keeps us safe for real regressions.

ops-bot: runbook updated by @marta: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rate-limit-waveform

priya: timeline: RFC by Tue EOD, PR for alert rules by Thu, staging deploy Fri, 48h monitor, prod rollout following Mon if green. Owners: priya (RFC + PR), owen (replay tests), sam (SLO override + rollback).

sam: i'll add a Grafana tile showing baseline, spikes, and paged vs suppressed counts. helps validate results quickly.

owen: i'll run a replay of last 30 days of rate-limit events through the new dedupe and threshold logic and post expected reduction numbers.

marta: action recap: priya -> RFC & PR; owen -> replay + tests; sam -> dashboard + SLO override; marta -> runbook + exceptions. target: PR merged Thu EOD.

priya: thanks. aim is to cut 2am pages by ~80% while preserving true failures. reconvene Mon 10am post-deploy to review metrics. :thumbsup:
